title: Heuristic shadowing experiments — logbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a messy running log for quick experiments where we 'shadow' automatic heuristics against human labelers. Goal is to find systematic gaps, borderline cases, and candidate rules we can safely apply in autopilot or as pre-filters for the labeling UI. Not a finished playbook — iterative notes, examples, failures, and micro-decisions.

Context / motivation:
- Our bulk cleanup runs make decent precision gains but miss small-context edgecases that human labelers catch.
- Shadowing = run heuristic prediction alongside labeler, but do NOT surface to end labeler. Collect mismatches, disagreement reasons, and sample counts.
- Want quick heuristics that are high-precision, explainable, and cheap to compute at ingest.

Experiment setup (how we ran things):
- Data slice: 15k random rows from recent ingestion (mix of short utterances, product titles, email-like strings, and free text).
- Heuristics tested in parallel: phone-sim, sku-pattern, punctuation-bias, email-outline, url-id-stripper, emoji-as-signal.
- Labelers: 2 full-time curators on rotation (Evan + Talia) doing a 200-sample adjudication pool each round.
- Metrics recorded per-sample: heuristic_output, labeler_label, time_to_label, disagreement_flag, freeform_reason (labeler typed short note).

Quick glossary (for the log):
- TPH = heuristic true-positive (matches labeler positive)
- FPH = heuristic false-positive (heuristic fired, labeler no)
- UNK = heuristic abstained / N/A

Round 1 notes (2024-11-12):
- phone-sim: regex target = variants of "\+?\d{1,3}[\s-]?(\(\d+\))?\s*\d{3}[\s-]?\d{3,4}".
  - Observed FPH when strings like "Order 411-333" or product codes "+1-800-412-333X" were mis-tagged. Labelers wrote: "looks like SKU or order id, not phone".
  - Decision: tighten post-digit heuristics — require grouping pattern (3-3 or 3-4) AND presence of separators or leading country code. Add negative-list of common sku prefixes (ORD, REF, SKU).

- sku-pattern: lightweight pattern for alphanum sequences 5-12 with internal hyphens/prefixes.
  - TP strong on catalog titles ("SKU-XL-7782") but brittle on human names that include alphas+digits "Juli3".
  - Labeler note: "when in sentence, treat as token; when token is isolated (start/end) treat as SKU candidate".
  - Rule proposal: require uppercase majority OR punctuation structure ("SKU-") to auto-tag.

Round 2 notes (2024-11-20):
- emoji-as-signal: heuristics that tag presence of emoji near greetings as likely 'sign-off' or 'tone' labels.
  - Corner cases: emoji inside product names ("Scented Candle 🕯️") should NOT imply sign-off.
  - Labelers flagged: "emoji can't be decisive without POS context".
  - Suggestion: debounce by co-occurrence with line breaks or punctuation typical of signatures ("--", "Thanks,") before leaning on emoji as sign-off.

- url-id-stripper: stripping trailing ids in urls ("/p/12345?ref=abc") and trying to map to normalized canonical.
  - Failure mode: stripping turned "/p/12-34" into "/p/12" because of naive split on dash.
  - Fix: use token-aware split, prefer longest numeric cluster, and test against list of known path patterns from sample.

Representative borderline examples (copied verbatim from labeler notes):
1) "Invoice +1 (555) 333-2124x" — labeler: PHONE? yes; heuristic: PHONE with extension. Issue: trailing 'x' variants.
2) "Order-ref: SKU-A12-1014" — labeler: SKU; phone heuristic fired once.
3) "Thanks! 😀" — labeler: SIGN_OFF false (emoji is inline), heuristic flagged sign-off in 18/50 similar samples.
4) "Javi3 Rey" — labeler: PERSON; sku-pattern flagged. Suggest token-case sensitivity.
5) "support@company.co.uk" — labeler: EMAIL; email-outline sometimes missed domains with double TLDs.

Mini decision log (changes to apply next run):
- phone-sim: require either international leading + or separators + length buckets; add negative-list for tokens starting with ORD/REF/SKU/PUR.
- sku-pattern: require either uppercase token ratio > 0.6 OR prefix match (SKU|ITEM|ID-).
- emoji-as-signal: don't use alone; require co-occurrence with line-boundary or signature tokens.
- url-id-stripper: prefer greedy numeric cluster; preserve dash-coded tokens unless explicitly matched to pattern.

Shadowing heuristics performance snapshot (small):
- 1. phone-sim: precision ~0.82, recall ~0.63 (lots of false positives on skus)
- 2. sku-pattern: precision ~0.76, recall ~0.58
- 3. emoji-as-signal: precision ~0.69, recall ~0.21 (low recall — many sign-offs without emoji)
- Note: numbers are from quick 500-sample pilot (no weighting).

Open questions / lanes for research:
- Should we maintain a curated negative-list (ORD, INV, PO) centrally or derive from frequency? Tradeoffs: manual curation vs noisy auto-extraction.
- How much complexity to add vs label ergonomics? Over-aggressive heuristics reduce labeling time but increase trust issues.
- Can we add a lightweight context window (3 tokens) to heuristics without costing latency at ingest?

Quick ACL for autoparking heuristics (when to auto-apply):
- autoplace = only when heuristic precision >= 0.9 in relevant slice AND FPH rate < 5% in last 10k queries; otherwise surface as pre-suggest in UI.

Small checklist for next run (2025-01-10):
- [ ] implement neg-list for phone-sim and re-run on fresh 10k sample
- [ ] add uppercase-ratio check to sku-pattern, test on product titles vs names
- [ ] add line-boundary detection to emoji-as-signal rule set
- [ ] gather 200 more samples of double-TLD emails and track failures
- [ ] export disagreement freeform reasons to Confluence page for pattern mining

Notes to self (quick heuristics-level ideas):
- use positional priors: tokens at end-of-line more likely to be signatures, tokens in isolated parentheses more likely to be phone/numeric ids.
- keep a small whitelist of known brand suffixes to avoid mis-tagging product titles as emotional/signature markers.
- when in doubt, abstain — surface to labeler rather than overwrite.

Final quick sample (for copy/paste into ticket):
Title: Tighten phone heuristic with negative-list and grouping rules
Description: phone-sim heuristic currently mislabels order ids and SKU-like tokens. Proposal: require either a leading + or consistent separator grouping (3-3 or 3-4) and reject tokens prefixed by ORD/REF/SKU/INV. Backfill a 50k sample to measure delta.
Acceptance criteria: precision improves to >=0.9 on randomized 5k sample, FPH rate < 2% for the orders slice.

(End of logbook entry — this file is intentionally informal; move stable rules to Confluence when vetted.)
